translations.source_sense_description: Kartografie, Geografie, von Landkarten: nach Norden ausrichten

glosses: Usually preceded by the: alternative letter-case form of Orient (“a region or a part of the world to the east of a certain place; countries of Asia, the East (especially East Asia)”)

examples.text: I, from the orient to the drooping weſt, / Making the wind my poſthorſe, ſtill unfold / The acts commenced on this ball of earth: […]
God planted Paradise in Eden, in the orients; and placed there the man whom he had formed.
I pitch my tent upon the naked sands, / And the tall palm, that plumes the orient lands, / Can with its beauty satisfy my heart.

glosses: The part of the horizon where the sun first appears in the morning; the east.

examples.text:

glosses: A pearl originating from the Indian region, reputed to be of great brilliance; (by extension) any pearl of particular beauty and value.

examples.text: The chambers of the East are opened in every land, and the sun comes forth to sow the earth with orient pearl.

glosses: The brilliance or colour of a high-quality pearl.

glosses: Of, facing, or located in the east; eastern, oriental.

glosses: Of a pearl or other gem: of great brilliance and value; (by extension) bright, lustrous.

glosses: To build or place (something) so as to face eastward.

examples.text: The first kind of interment was that of leaden coffins, rectangular in shape, covered with a lid, occupying deeper graves than any of the other interments, more or less accurately oriented, sometimes containing coins, as of the Emperor Gratian (ob. 383), and sometimes not. [...] The second type of interment, also of Romans or Romanised Britons, resembled the first in being more or less perfectly oriented, the orientation varying, probably according as it had taken place in summer or in winter, from E.N.E. to E.S.E. over about 45°; [...]

glosses: To align or place (a person or object) so that his, her, or its east side, north side, etc., is positioned toward the corresponding points of the compass; (specifically, surveying) to rotate (a map attached to a plane table) until the line of direction between any two of its points is parallel to the corresponding direction in nature.

examples.text: Without a compass the table is oriented, when set at one end of a line previously determined, by sighting back on this line, [...]. To orient the table, when at a station unconnected with others, is more difficult.

glosses: To direct towards or point at a particular direction.

examples.text: The workers oriented all the signs to face the road.
